headword: ニュース{速報|そくほう}

definitions.gloss: breaking news; news flash; news bulletin
definitions.explanation: An urgent news report broadcast immediately when an important event occurs, interrupting regular programming or appearing as an alert.

examples.japanese: ニュース{速報|そくほう}が{入|はい}った。
examples.english: A breaking news report just came in.

examples.japanese: スマホにニュース{速報|そくほう}の{通知|つうち}が{届|とど}いた。
examples.english: A breaking news notification arrived on my smartphone.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}のニュース{速報|そくほう}が{流|なが}れた{途端|とたん}、{家族|かぞく}に{連絡|れんらく}を{取|と}ろうとしたが{電話|でんわ}がつながらなかった。
examples.english: The moment the earthquake breaking news aired, I tried to contact my family but couldn't get through on the phone.

notes:
A compound of ニュース (news) and {速報|そくほう} (bulletin, flash report). In Japan, ニュース{速報|そくほう} typically appears as a text banner across the top or bottom of the TV screen, accompanied by a distinctive chime sound. It is used for earthquakes, major political events, severe weather warnings, and other urgent developments.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ニュース{速報|そくほう}が{入|はい}る: a news flash comes in
- ニュース{速報|そくほう}が{流|なが}れる: a news flash airs/runs
- ニュース{速報|そくほう}の{通知|つうち}: breaking news notification
- ニュース{速報|そくほう}を{受|う}ける: to receive a news flash

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {速報|そくほう}: bulletin; flash report — the general term for any urgent report, not limited to news
- {号外|ごうがい}: newspaper extra — a special edition printed for breaking news
- {臨時|りんじ}ニュース: special news bulletin — an extended broadcast interrupting regular programming
